# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-20 (Extended v147)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826; **current narrative point (winter Year 5, early morning after escape night)**: Paris—Rue Plumet (Valjean's primary house); Rue de Babylone (secret passage exit); Luxembourg; Salpêtrière district; garden near Austerlitz settlement; Place de la Bastille (elephant monument under construction); Impasse de la Planchette (blind alley); Orme-Saint-Gervais district; Prison Charlemagne (New Building and Fine-Air top story); Rue des Ballets; Rue du Roi-de-Sicile; Rue Saint-Antoine; ruin wall of La Force; Ravenmere and other English provincial towns (Elmhaven, Ostcombe, Wilwick, Salcombe, Dunstead, etc.). **Seasonal progression**: Winter Year 5 environment (wintry gale, rain, thunder, showers, frost silvering hedges, muddy roads with ruts and puddles after thaw, smoke lying flat, salt and tar harbor smell, children chasing hoops, bees in lavender, vespers bells).

## Primary Locations
**RUE PLUMET HOUSE**: Single-story pavilion in deserted Rue Plumet with garden approximately one-and-a-half acres. Two ground-floor rooms, two first-floor chambers, downstairs kitchen, upstairs boudoir, attic. Behind pavilion: narrow courtyard, low building (two rooms, cellar). Secret-spring door masked in building communicates via long narrow paved winding corridor to Rue de Babylone quarter-league distant. Garden characteristics: Left uncultivated; breathes melancholy, solitude, liberty, absence of man, presence of God.

**PLACE DE LA BASTILLE & ELEPHANT MONUMENT**: Rough model, marvelous sketch of Napoleon's idea. Elephant forty feet high, constructed of timber and masonry, bearing tower resembling house, formerly painted green, now black. Broad brow, trunk, tusks, tower, crupper, four feet like columns produce surprising and terrible form under starry heavens. In 1832: enveloped in immense shirt of woodwork, surrounded by vast plank enclosure isolating structure. Gap in fence provides entry to enclosure. Timber-yard nearby with ladder for laborers.

**ELEPHANT'S INTERIOR (GAVROCHE'S REFUGE)**: Interior accessed via black hole in belly near foreleg. Vast hollow space resembling whale's belly. Long brown beam forming vertebral column with massive arching ribs. Stalactites of plaster like entrails; vast spiders' webs forming dirty diaphragms. **Rats swarming by thousands in elephant's carcass—frightened by voices but return when silent.** Three long poles thrust into floor rubbish consolidated at summits with rope forming pyramidal bundle. Trellis-work of brass wire enveloping poles, held by iron wire fastenings. Row of heavy stones keeping network down to floor. Grating creates cage-like enclosure. Gavroche's bed situated behind net.

**PRISON CHARLEMAGNE (NEW BUILDING)**: Ancient decrepit structure, weak point in prison system. Walls eaten by saltpetre; authorities forced to line dormitory vaults with wood sheathing because stones become detached and fall on prisoners' beds. Contains four dormitories, one above another, plus top story called "Bel-Air" (Fine-Air). Large chimney-flue from ancient kitchen of Dukes de la Force starts ground floor, traverses all four stories, cuts dormitories as flattened pillar, pierces roof. Roofers currently re-laying and re-jointing slates on prison, creating scaffoldings and ladders—bridges and stairs in direction of liberty. Saint-Bernard courtyard no longer absolutely isolated from Charlemagne and Saint-Louis courts.

**FINE-AIR (BEL-AIR TOP STORY)**: Large hall with Mansard roof, guarded with triple gratings and double doors of sheet iron, studded with enormous bolts. Four dormer-windows at north end. Facing windows at regular intervals: four square, tolerably vast cages, separated by narrow passages, built of masonry to about elbow height, rest to roof of iron bars. Lighted by skylight. Sentry relieved every two hours, marches up and down in front of cages with loaded musket. Jailer escorted by two dogs enters daily at four o'clock in afternoon, deposits loaf of black bread weighing two pounds, jug of water, bowl of thin bouillon with Mayagan beans, inspects irons, taps bars. Two visits during night. Prisoners wear fetters weighing fifty pounds.

**RUE DES BALLETS/RUE DU ROI-DE-SICILE RUIN**: Spot where in last century stood house; now only back wall remains, regular wall of masonry rising to height of third story. Two large square windows visible; middle one nearest right gable barred with worm-eaten beam as prop. Wall was fragment of outer wall of La Force. Empty space left by demolished house half-filled by fence of rotten boards shored up by five stone posts. Recess conceals little shanty leaning against ruin remnant. Fence has gate fastened only by latch. Steep escarpment three stories high separates ruin edge from pavement of street.

## Jean Valjean's Recovery and Mysterious Activity (October 1831—Winter Year 5)
**The wound and illness**: Day following Jondrette visit, Valjean appeared with large inflamed wound on left arm resembling burn (origin unclear). Detained in house one month with fever; refused doctor. Cosette deserted pavilion, devoted herself entirely to his care.

**March-April transformation**: Valjean convalesced; happiness reviving in ineffable rays; Luxembourg, young stranger Marius, Cosette's coldness—all clouds upon his soul growing dim.

**Charitable activities resumed**: Carry bread to hungry, clothing to cold. Cosette often accompanied Valjean on visits to poor.

**Mysterious journeys**: Valjean took occasional journeys at long intervals, absent one or two days utmost. Destination unknown, even to Cosette. Pattern: journeys typically when money lacking in house.

**Nocturnal garden activity and manuscript delivery**: Cosette observed figure walking beneath trees in garden dusk, carrying large club. Found stone on garden bench; became alarmed, fled, closed shutters. Later discovered packet of leaflets on garden bench—manuscript containing extended philosophical meditation on love as divine spark—immortal, incorruptible, infinite, burning to marrow of bones, beaming in depths of heaven.

## Marius and Cosette's Romance
**Cosette's recognition and revelation (autumn Year 5)**: Upon reading manuscript, recognized writer as Marius. Acknowledged she had never truly forgotten him, had always loved and adored him. "The fire had been smothered, and had smouldered for a time," but now "it had burst forth afresh, and had inflamed her whole being."

**Garden encounter (autumn Year 5)**: Marius grasped Cosette in garden as she fell. He took her in arms, pressed her close, "without knowing what he was doing." Supported her though tottering himself. They fell upon bench. Their lips met without knowing how. Night serene and splendid overhead. "Effusion followed silence, which is fulness." Two beings "pure as spirits" told each other everything—dreams, intoxications, ecstasies, chimæras, weaknesses. Confided how they had adored each other from afar, longed, despaired. "Their two hearts poured themselves out into each other in such wise, that at the expiration of a quarter of an hour, it was the young man who had the young girl's soul, and the young girl who had the young man's soul. Each became permeated with the other, they were enchanted with each other, they dazzled each other."

## Thénardiers and Child Substitution
**Family disruption**: Thénardiers in prison following Jondrette garret arrest.

**Magnon arrangement**: Before police raid, Thénardier handed two little sons to Magnon (fashionable woman in criminal sphere) with express intention of renouncing them forever. Magnon promised ten francs monthly, actually paid. M. Gillenormand (grandfather) continued compact—came every six months to see children, did not perceive change. Children well cared for, well clothed, adequately fed, treated almost like little gentlemen—better by false mother than real mother.

**Spring 1832 dispersal**: Shortly after Magnon handed note to Éponine, sudden police raid made in Rue Clocheperce. Magnon and Mamselle Miss (clever gallicized English thief, naturalized Parisienne, intimately connected with medals and diamonds) seized; house emptied. **Spring 1832: The two children set out alone**. Elder leading younger, holding paper with address **M. Barge, collector of rents, Rue du Roi-de-Sicile, No. 8**. At corner of Rue Clocheperce, gust of wind tore paper from elder's benumbed fingers; as night falling, child unable to find it again. **Lost in city, wandering in spring cold.**

## Gavroche and the Two Lost Children
**Gavroche's character and activities**: Street child, homeless, hungry, clever pickpocket. Stole Montparnasse's purse (late April Year 5). "Always shivering gayly under his rags." Wears woman's woollen shawl picked up unknown where, converted into neck comforter. Engages in "shaving barbers"—stealing cakes of soap from shop-fronts to sell for sou to hair-dressers in suburbs.

**Encounter with two lost children (spring 1832)**: While scrutinizing wig-maker's shop window near Orme-Saint-Gervais, observed two children of unequal stature, very neatly dressed, smaller than himself—one about seven years old, other five. Both timidly entered shop with plaintive request. Barber wheeled round furiously, thrust back elder with left hand and younger with knee, slammed door. Gavroche observed beggar-girl, thirteen or fourteen years old, lying chilled under porte-cochère.

**Rescue and shelter (spring-to-winter Year 5)**: Gavroche provided bread and promised shelter. Led two children through gap in fence into elephant's enclosure at Place de la Bastille. Raised ladder from timber-yard and placed against elephant's foreleg. Climbed to black hole in elephant's belly with remarkable agility. Reappeared pale like wan whitish spectre at shadowy hole. Elder child undertook risk of climbing; younger felt greatly inclined to cry but did not dare. Gavroche descended with agility of monkey, grasped child of five, planted him on ladder middle, climbed behind him.

**Winter Year 5 nocturnal incident**: Five-year-old boy heard hubbub overhead (possibly rat attack during darkness), jogged elder brother's elbow. Elder had already shut eyes as Gavroche ordered. Younger brother questioned Gavroche in low tone with bated breath. **Gavroche grasped little fellow's hand across his brother; child felt reassured.** Courage and strength communicated mysteriously. Silence reigned; sound of voices frightened rats off. Within few minutes rats returned raging but in vain—three little fellows fell fast asleep, heard nothing more. Wintry gale mingled with rain blew in gusts; patrol searched doorways, alleys, enclosures, passed in silence before elephant. Monster sheltered from heaven and men the three poor sleeping children.

## Prison Escape: Brujon and Guelemer (Winter Year 5, Night of Early Morning)
**Brujon's background**: Dangerous prisoner with appearance of delicate health and profoundly premeditated languor. Polished, intelligent sprig and thief with caressing glance and atrocious smile. First studies in art directed to roofs. Made great progress in industry of men who tear off lead, plunder roofs, despoil gutters by process called "double pickings."

**Thénardier's confinement**: **Rated as burglar, detained as measure of precaution under charge of organizing nocturnal ambush with armed force, kept in sight in one of four cages in Fine-Air since night of 3d of February.** Kept on feet fetters weighing fifty pounds. Obtained permission to keep iron bolt to spike bread into wall crack "to preserve it from rats." Procured and secreted bottle of wine with narcotic invented by Desrues, rendered famous by band of _Endormeurs_ (Sleep-compellers). Sentry relieved every two hours marched in front of cage with loaded musket.

**Night of escape**: **When Gavroche picked up two lost children, Brujon and Guelemer, who knew Babet had escaped that morning and waited in street along with Montparnasse, rose softly and with nail Brujon had found, began to pierce chimney against which their beds stood.** Rubbish fell on Brujon's bed, unheard. Showers mingled with thunder shook doors on hinges, created terrible and opportune uproar. Prisoners who woke pretended to fall asleep, left Guelemer and Brujon to devices. Before sound reached watcher sleeping in grated cell opening into dormitory, wall pierced, chimney scaled, iron grating barring upper orifice of flue forced, two redoubtable ruffians on roof. Wind and rain redoubled, roof slippery.

**Roof-to-street escape**: Abyss six feet broad and eighty feet deep separated them from surrounding wall. Sentinel's musket gleamed through gloom at bottom. Fastened rope Brujon spun in dungeon to stumps of iron bars just wrenched off, flung other over outer wall, crossed abyss at one bound, clung to coping of wall, got astride of it, let themselves slip one after other along rope upon little roof touching bath-house, pulled rope after them, jumped down into courtyard of bath-house, traversed it, pushed open porter's wicket, pulled rope, opened porte-cochère, found themselves in street. **Successfully escaped.**

**Thénardier's escape**: At two o'clock in morning, old soldier sentinel relieved and replaced by conscript. Few moments later, man with dogs paid visit, went off without noticing except possibly excessive youth and "rustic air" of "raw recruit." Two hours afterwards, at four o'clock, when came to relieve conscript, he was found asleep on floor lying like log near Thénardier's cage. **Thénardier no longer there. Hole in ceiling of cage and above it hole in roof. One plank of bed wrenched off, probably carried away.** Half-empty bottle containing remains of stupefying wine seized in cell. **Soldier's bayonet disappeared.** At all events, **Thénardier dripping with perspiration, drenched with rain, clothes hanging in ribbons, hands flayed, elbows bleeding, knees torn, had reached edge of wall of ruin; there stretched himself out at full length; there his strength had failed him. Steep escarpment three stories high separated him from pavement of street.**

## Supporting Characters and Provincial Elements
**Father Mabeuf**: Old man in Austerlitz settlement garden; capable of extraordinary physical prowess despite age; defeated Montparnasse in unexpected reversal (late April Year 5).

**Montparnasse**: Elegant ruffian, eighteen years old; rose in mouth; well-dressed in fine black coat; unexpectedly defeated by Father Mabeuf; thief victim of Gavroche; warned Gavroche of police; currently escaped from prison (escaped morning of night when Brujon escaped).

**Lieutenant Théodule**: Handsome officer of lancers, apparently eighteen or younger; vain, insolent; passed Rue Plumet gate autumn Year 5; smiled at Cosette (she found him insipid, silly, stupid, useless, foppish, displeasing, impertinent, extremely ugly).

**Toussaint**: House servant; fastens shutters; terrifies Cosette with melodrama about assassins.

**Marius**: Young stranger from Luxembourg; author of philosophical manuscript on divine love; present in garden autumn Year 5 for encounter with Cosette; recognized her from Luxembourg meetings.

**Magnon's associate**: Mamselle Miss—clever gallicized English thief, naturalized Parisienne, seized in Rue Clocheperce police raid.

**Guelemer**: Criminal associate of Brujon in New Building; represents "crime"; escaped with Brujon on night of escape.

**Babet**: Escaped same morning prisoners Brujon and Guelemer escaped.

**Provincial figures**: Semor Brackick in Ravenmere (complained of aching back, sorted old letters by candlelight, bought ribbon, argued with carter, laughed at story, mended torn sleeve, fell asleep before fire caught); Yewyn Haskick in Ravenmere (quit Ravenmere for good after quarrel, took lodgings in Salcombe); Jotho Thornmere received pewter dagger from youngest son of Nelan Brackick; Islan and Vesmira Thornmere moved from Elmhaven to Ostcombe.

## Key States
- **Cosette's emotional state** (autumn Year 5 through winter Year 5): Transformed from confusion and terror to luminous joy upon discovering Marius's manuscript. Fire of love reignited. Exchanged intimate conversation with Marius; hearts poured into each other; became permeated with each other, enchanted, dazzled.
- **Two lost Thénardier children** (spring 1832 through winter Year 5): **Now sheltered by Gavroche inside Place de la Bastille elephant monument, winter Year 5 early morning. Five-year-old terrified by hubbub (possibly rats), reassured by Gavroche's hand-grasp. All three fell fast asleep during wintry gale and rain.**
- **Thénardier** (winter Year 5 early morning): **Escaped from Fine-Air cage early morning winter Year 5. Currently exhausted, reached edge of wall of ruin at Rue des Ballets/Rue du Roi-de-Sicile; strength failed him. Separated from street pavement below by steep three-story escarpment. Status: escaped prisoner on ruin edge, unable to descend further.**
- **Brujon and Guelemer**: **Successfully escaped from Prison Charlemagne New Building via roof, chimney, rope across abyss, bath-house courtyard, escaped into street winter Year 5 early morning.**
- **Babet and Montparnasse**: Babet escaped morning of prison escape night; Montparnasse waited in street for Brujon and Guelemer (confirmed escaped from prison).
- **Season**: Winter Year 5, early morning. Wintry gale, rain with thunder, frost silvering hedges, muddy roads with ruts and puddles after thaw, smoke lying flat, salt and tar harbor smell, children chasing hoops, bees in lavender, vespers bells.
